title: Keep a filed inspection as it was filed

blocks.text: Site inspections are filed as evidence. Last week an auditor found an inspection of dock 7 dated 1 January 1970, and another whose list of defects no longer matched the inspector's notes. The weekly report rounds the dates it is given, and the compliance export rewrites defect names in the lists it reads.

`Inspection` keeps its date as a `java.util.Date` and its defects as a `String[]`, and its constructor already keeps copies of what it was given. Finish the two getters in `src/main/java/practice/Inspection.java`, `getInspectedAt()` and `getDefects()`, so that nothing a caller does with what they return changes a filed inspection. About two lines in total.

cases.says: an inspection reports its site, its date and its defects in the order they were found
changing the Date a caller got back leaves the inspection's date as it was
setting an element of the defect list a caller got back leaves the inspection's defects as they were

origin.section: A Getter That Returns a Date or an Array Hands Out the Field

concepts: Arrays.asList copies nothing: set on the list it returns writes into the array.
A getter that returns a Date or an array field hands the caller the object's own field, private final or not; it returns a copy, or the class stores an immutable type.
